one_month_reasoning: ON's Q3 2026 report is still only estimated for ~2026-11-02 (Alpha Vantage/MarketBeat; onsemi has not posted a date and its IR site returned 503 when I checked), so it most likely falls just after the 2026-10-29 window, with a small chance of an earlier in-window date. In-window events: the Oct 27-28 FOMC (decision Oct 28, ~69% hike odds on Kalshi/Polymarket per the supervisor's check, which I missed in round 1). A hike is largely priced, so it adds variance more than drift for a high-beta semi. Late-October analog/power peer prints (TXN, NXPI, STM) set auto/industrial sentiment, and merger-arb pressure from the Synaptics deal continues. None of this gives me a directional edge, so I use a symmetric lognormal centred on the $75.95 spot. I widened the monthly sigma slightly to ~17% (64% realized / 3.5 = 18%) to allow for the FOMC and a possible early earnings date.

fair_value.method: Equal blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ~$5.00 x 16x = $80) and FCF yield (NTM FCF ~$2.05B on ~450M post-deal shares = $4.56/share at a 6% yield = $76). Both now use lower inputs than round 1: capex normalises from trough levels and I take a small haircut for SiC pricing pressure.

inputs_detail.value: Mgmt: pricing actions offset material cost increases; China auto SiC revenue +60-70% y/y in 2026; SiC AI-DC revenue +~60% in 2026

inputs_detail.derivation: CY27 $4.53 grown ~20% for CY28 (the analyst-day framework says operating income grows more than 2x as fast as revenue), which puts NTM standalone at ~$5.40. Less ~4% for first-year Synaptics dilution (accretive only within ~18 months) = ~$5.20, which was my round-1 figure. Less a further ~4% for SiC device-margin pressure from low-cost Chinese wafers (TrendForce; Czech job cuts). Management says its price increases track material costs and China SiC share is rising, so I take a partial haircut rather than the 7-10% some peers used: ~$5.00.

$75.95 / CY27 consensus $4.53 = 16.8x. At the June $120 VWAP in the S-4 the stock traded ~26x. The deal overhang, a hiking Fed and cyclicality argue for staying near today's de-rated multiple, so 16x NTM.

inputs_detail.value: Capex 2.7% of revenue in 2026E rising to ~5% by 2030; FCF margin 24.8% in 2026E, 30-35% target for 2030

inputs_detail.derivation: CY27 consensus revenue $7.42B x ~25% FCF margin = $1.85B. Operating leverage lifts the margin, but capex steps up from 2.7% toward ~3.5% in 2027 on the analyst-day glide path to 5%, so the margin stays near 2026E's 24.8% rather than my round-1 27%. Rolling forward half a year gives ~$1.95B. Add Synaptics FCF net of integration costs, with synergies back-loaded, ~$0.10B.
395M Q3 diluted guide less ~2%/yr buybacks ($5.3B authorization left; policy is to return 100% of FCF) = ~390M, grossed up ~13.6% for the Synaptics issuance (88/12 pro forma) = ~445-450M.
At $75.95 (~$30B cap) the LTM FCF yield is ~5% on trough capex. I require 6% on NTM for cyclical and merger risk. $2.05B / 450M = $4.56; $4.56 / 0.06 = $76.
~$1.3/share; immaterial and ignored in the yield calc.

bear.story: The analog/auto cycle rolls over in 2027 after the pricing and restock bump, and Chinese SiC competition squeezes device margins. Gross margin stalls near 40% and capex normalises, so FCF falls to ~$1.6B. Synaptics integration or regulatory delay keeps arbitrage pressure on. ~12x on ~$4.00 EPS.

base.story: Utilization climbs toward 90%, price increases offset material costs, and GM reaches the mid-40s by mid-2027. CY27 EPS ~$4.5 and NTM ~$5.0 after the SiC haircut. Synaptics closes mid-2027 roughly neutral; the multiple stays ~16x.

bull.story: AI data center roughly doubles again in 2027, 800VDC/SiC wins broaden and book-to-bill stays above 1. GM tracks the 53% 2030 path; NTM EPS ~$5.7 re-rates to ~21x as the Fed pauses and the deal overhang clears.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$52 the stock would trade ~11.5x CY27 consensus EPS ($4.53) and at a ~7-8% yield on normalised (~25% margin) 2027 FCF, levels normally seen only near cycle troughs. Getting there most likely requires a guidance cut (a booking reversal, utilization falling back from 83%, pricing not sticking, or a SiC price war hitting device margins) or a failed or renegotiated Synaptics deal, not ordinary 50-60% volatility. It sits ~20% below the $65.80-66.60 post-analyst-day low.

key_uncertainties: Is the 2026 demand upturn (book-to-bill >1, lead times 27->32 weeks) durable, or a restock- and pricing-driven bump?
Gross margin path: 83% utilization, where each 1pt moves GM 25-30bp; 2026E GM 40.3% vs the 53% 2030 target; SiC device margins under Chinese wafer price pressure
Capex normalisation from trough levels (1.8% of revenue in H1 2026, 2.7% for 2026E) toward 5% by 2030, which cuts FCF conversion
Synaptics deal: the 1.35x ratio sat above several fairness ranges at ON's $120 VWAP; regulatory timing to mid-2027; accretion only within ~18 months
Macro: a hiking Fed (Oct 28) is a headwind for high-beta semiconductor multiples

reasoning: Round 2. Primary filings frame the setup. Q2 2026 (8-K, Aug 3): revenue $1,604M (+9% y/y), non-GAAP GM 39.3%, EPS $0.74, FCF $425M, but on capex of only $34.3M (2.1% of revenue; H1 1.8%). The supervisor was right that my round-1 27% FCF margin capitalised trough capex. The analyst-day deck shows capex of 2.7% of revenue in 2026E rising to ~5% by 2030, and a 24.8% FCF margin in 2026E. I now use ~25% for 2027, which cuts NTM FCF from $2.2B to ~$2.05B. The supervisor assumed capex jumps to ~5% at once; I think that overstates the 2027 hit, because management's own path is gradual. On EPS I keep consensus as the anchor, since it was revised up over 30-90 days and the Q2 call says price increases offset material costs, with China auto SiC revenue up 60-70%. I still take a ~4% haircut for Chinese SiC wafer price pressure on device margins, which gives NTM EPS $5.00 vs $5.20. Fair value falls from $82 to $78 (16x $5.00 = $80; 6% yield on $4.56 FCF/share = $76), about 3% above spot. Scenarios: bear $48 (25%), base $79 (50%), bull $120 (25%), mean ~$81.5, with a hiking Fed adding to bear risk. The 12-month ladder is roughly lognormal with median ~$77 and sigma ~0.52, a bit below round 1 across the middle strikes. The 1-month ladder stays symmetric around spot with a slightly wider sigma for the in-window Oct 28 FOMC. Research this round: 4 lookups (Q2 8-K cash flow, analyst-day 425 capex path, Q2 call SiC commentary, Q3 date check).
